memory_candidates.content: Bash gotcha: `while IFS= read -r line; do ...; done < <(printf '%s' "$str" | some_transform)` silently skips the body for the LAST (or only) line whenever the piped output lacks a trailing newline, because `read` returns nonzero on that final partial read even though it populates the variable. Fix: use `printf '%s\n' "$str"` (note the explicit \n) before piping into any line-based consumer (`tr`, `read` loops, etc.). This produced a real defect during implementation: a hook's segment-classification loop never executed its body at all, so every command was vacuously classified as trivial.

When writing a Bash-command-classifying hook (e.g. detecting trivial/no-op commands), do NOT reuse guard-destructive-git.sh's quote-blanking technique verbatim if the classification depends on content INSIDE quotes (e.g. whether an echo argument contains $/backtick for expansion). Quote-blanking is correct only when quoted content is inherently safe free text to ignore (e.g. commit messages); for a command whose quoted arguments are the actual executed/printed content, scan the raw (non-blanked) text for danger characters instead, and treat segment-splitting-only quote-safety as a separate, smaller concern with its own accepted (safe-direction) blind spot.
